style: Original illustration made to look like a hand-printed RISOGRAPH poster: only four flat spot inks — fluorescent orange, deep federal-blue/navy, warm mustard yellow and off-black — on cream uncoated paper. Visible coarse halftone dots, slight misregistration between ink layers (1-2 mm offset), uneven ink coverage, paper grain and tiny dust specks. Drawing done with confident brush-and-ink linework like a traditional Korean folk painting (minhwa) woodblock: the tiger has the old minhwa character — big round goggle eyes, wide toothy comical grin, bold blunt stripes, chunky stylised paws — drawn as flat shapes, not realistic fur. People drawn simply with few lines, matte flat color, small simple faces. Composition asymmetric and graphic with generous negative space; strong silhouette readable from far. Leave the top 24% of the frame as flat dark navy ink with only a little texture (title space) and keep the bottom 9% flat navy too. AVOID: glossy highlights, 3D rendering, airbrushed gradients, oversaturated neon, bokeh, lens flare, perfectly symmetrical layout, plastic-looking skin, excessive micro-detail, cluttered backgrounds. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, numbers, signage writing, fake glyphs, watermarks, logos or app interface anywhere; phone screens are plain flat yellow-white light. Hands simple with correct finger count or hidden in pockets/sleeves. Not in the style of any specific artist.

images.en: A steep zigzag stairway in an old hillside Seoul neighbourhood at night, seen from slightly below and to the left. Small flat-roofed houses with rooftop water tanks stacked up the hill, a few thin power lines, a flat full moon off-centre. One tired young office worker in a long padded coat climbs the stairs, head bowed into the phone held in both hands, not noticing anything. On three landings going up (big in the foreground right, medium in the middle, small near the top) sits the same minhwa tiger in an oversized hoodie. Each tiger holds one chunky paw out toward her PALM-UP AND EMPTY, demanding, with a sly sideways grin, half-lidded scheming eyes and the tip of its tongue licking its lips — friendly-looking but clearly a con artist. Beside each tiger lies a small neat stack of round white rice cakes (tteok) it has already collected; the stacks grow taller the higher the landing. Her open tote bag holds just one last rice cake. A thin trail of rice-cake crumbs runs down the steps behind her.

Bold vertical poster composition: a giant minhwa tiger in an oversized hoodie lies across the top of a mountain pass, chin on one paw, sly half-lidded grin; the mountain ridges below it are actually a few huge dark smartphones stacked at angles like folded hills in a Korean landscape painting, their screens flat pale yellow. A single winding path climbs over the phone-ridges from a tiny lone commuter with a basket at the bottom left; along the path round white rice cakes (tteok) are laid at intervals, getting fewer toward the top, and the last one sits right in front of the tiger's open paw, palm-up. Two stylised minhwa pine trees frame the lower corners. Large flat moon upper right inside the navy title area is acceptable but keep it small.
